newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends softer amid light trading.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends softer amid light trading.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed slightly weaker at 28.650 to the dollar on Tuesday from 28.60 amid light trading, traders said.
One trader said there was still dollar demand from corporate clients, although it was tempered when the central bank sold dollars at 28.85 early in the session.
He estimated the central bank to have sold as much as $10.5 million out of the $25 million traded in the market.
Another trader said some banks were also on the selling side as they anticipated a large foreign exchange inflow from a local corporation.
The peso crept up from 28.85 at the opening to close at 28.65.
The parallel rate was hovering between 28.80 and 28.95 in the morning.

The Bankers Association of the Philippines earlier said it had lifted the two percent ceiling it set for banks' over-the-counter dollar sale since the rate had already stabilised in the current range.
